papers.title: Lymphatic Reconstructive Surgery in Primary and Secondary Lymphedema: A Comparative Outcome Study.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Primary lymphedema (PLE) presumably results from an abnormal development of the lymphatic system. Current PLE management strategies are mainly rooted on practice algorithms well established for secondary lymphedema (SLE). The effectiveness of lymphovenous anastomosis (LVA) in PLE is an ongoing debate. METHODS: Patients recorded in the University Hospital Zurich database with PLE or SLE who underwent LVA and/or vascularized lymph node transfer (VLNT) between 2016 and 2023 were analyzed. Limb volumes were evaluated preoperatively and at specific postoperative time points, comparing outcomes after different surgical procedures and their combination. RESULTS: Fourty-eight limbs met the inclusion criteria for this study. In PLE patients, LVA alone showed significantly less effective results in the change of limb volume than VLNT alone (P = 0.035). LVA only reduced limb volume in 25% of treated patients, whereas VLNT only or VLNT in combination with LVA reduced limb volumes in 70% and 54.5% of treated patients. Concerning patients experiencing an actual reduction in limb volume, LVA alone lead to a limb volume reduction of 3.46% in PLE patients and 3.72% in SLE patients, whereas VLNT alone showed a median reduction of 5.36% and 7.98% in PLE and SLE patients, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Executing LVA alone seems to be less effective than executingVLNT alone. Consequently, in PLE patients we encourage to execute VLNT primarily, along with intraoperative Indocyanine-green-angiography-guided decision-making regarding the implementation of additional LVA.

papers.title: Gelatinous drop-like amyloid in FOXC2 distichiasis syndrome: a case report.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Gelatinous drop-like dystrophy is a rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the TACSTD2 gene and characterized by subepithelial amyloid deposits in the cornea. Alterations in FOXC2 are seen in lymphedema-distichiasis syndrome, in which patients classically exhibit lymphedema of the extremities and a double row of eyelashes. This report links alterations in the FOXC2 gene to a corneal phenotype that is histologically identical to that seen in gelatinous drop-like dystrophy. CASE PRESENTATION: A 14-year-old male with congenital distichiasis presented with chronic photosensitivity and progressively worsening vision over several years. On examination, gelatinous-appearing lesions were observed on the inferior third of each cornea with neovascularization. Genetic testing identified a likely pathogenic alteration in FOXC2, a gene linked to lymphedema-distichiasis syndrome. No genetic alterations of corneal dystrophy were identified. The patient underwent excisions of the corneal lesions with simple limbal epithelial transplant, amniotic membrane transplant and temporary central tarsorrhaphy. The pathologic features of the corneal lesions resembled gelatinous drop-like dystrophy. One side was free of inflammation, while the other side showed a granulomatous response to the amyloid, which is unusual in this site. Potential pathogenic and clearance mechanisms are discussed. There has been no recurrence of the corneal lesions in approximately 3 years of follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: This case presents a new link between FOXC2 alterations and a histological phenotype that resembles gelatinous drop-like dystrophy (GDLD-like), emphasizing the importance of clinical, pathologic, and molecular correlation. Granulomatous responses to amyloid are unusual in this immune privileged site.

papers.title: Effective Management Strategies for Primary Lymphedema of the Lower Extremities: Integrating Conservative and Surgical Therapies in Early and Late Stages
papers.abstract: Lymphedema results from abnormalities in the lymphatic system. Primary lymphedema stems from malformations in lymphatic vessels or nodes, characterized by progressive tissue fibrosis following repetitive inflammation. Presents a comprehensive approach to treating primary lymphedema integrating conservative and surgical therapies at early and late stages.
papers.what_happened: A review in Microsurgery synthesizes conservative and surgical management approaches for primary lower extremity lymphedema across disease stages.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides a structured clinical framework for primary lymphedema management combining physiotherapy and reconstructive surgery.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Narrative review pooling heterogeneous case series without systematic meta-analytic rigor; all cited surgical evidence is single-arm and retrospective.

papers.title: Lipomatosis of Nerve Misdiagnosed as Primary Lymphedema: Report of Two Cases
papers.abstract: Primary lymphedema and lipomatosis of nerve are distinct conditions causing significant limb overgrowth but differ in pathophysiology and treatment. Two case studies highlighting diagnostic differentiation challenges.
papers.what_happened: A two-case report describes lipomatosis of nerve being initially misdiagnosed as primary lymphedema.
papers.why_it_matters: Clinically actionable differential diagnosis: misdiagnosis can lead to inappropriate therapy.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Two cases only; no systematic series to estimate misdiagnosis frequency.

papers.title: Genetic Study of HGF-MET Signaling Pathway in Primary Lymphedema Patients: Supporting Evidence for Loss of Function Variants in HGF
papers.abstract: Study explores genetic basis of primary lymphedema in an Italian cohort, focusing on HGF/MET signaling pathway genes. Analysis identified 8 variants in HGF, MET, and CBL genes among unrelated patients, with seven variants previously unreported.
papers.what_happened: Retrospective genetic analysis of 408 Italian primary lymphedema patients identified 8 variants (7 previously unreported) in HGF, MET, and CBL genes.
papers.why_it_matters: HGF-MET signaling expands the potential diagnostic gene panel beyond established genes.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective; computational pathogenicity only; Italian cohort founder effects possible.

papers.title: Case Report: Surgical management of primary lymphedema with a novel PROX1 mutation involving upper and lower limbs
papers.abstract: Case report describing novel heterozygous PROX1 mutation (c.1019C>G, p.S340C) in a 59-year-old male with primary lymphedema affecting both upper and lower extremities.
papers.what_happened: Novel PROX1 variant (c.1019C>G, p.S340C) in bilateral primary lymphedema managed with combined surgery and conservative therapy.
papers.why_it_matters: Novel PROX1 variants expand mutational spectrum and genotype-phenotype understanding.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case; variant not functionally validated.

papers.title: Similarities and differences in the clinical features and management of primary lymphedema and kaposiform hemangioendothelioma associated with lymphedema in children
papers.abstract: Study examines clinical features, imaging, treatments, and outcomes of 12 pediatric primary lymphedema and 12 kaposiform hemangioendothelioma-related lymphedema patients.
papers.what_happened: Retrospective comparison of 12 pediatric primary LE and 12 KHE-associated LE patients found distinct presentations and treatment responses.
papers.why_it_matters: KHE requires specific treatment (sirolimus, vincristine) fundamentally different from primary lymphedema management.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Small n (12+12); single-center; Chinese population.

papers.title: A rare case of primary lymphedema tarda in an elderly Filipino — Diagnostic and management considerations
papers.journal: Journal of Clinical Images and Medical Case Reports
papers.abstract: Case report of primary lymphedema tarda presenting in an elderly Filipino patient.
papers.what_happened: Late-onset primary lymphedema (lymphedema tarda) in an elderly Filipino patient.
papers.why_it_matters: Highlights that primary lymphedema can present at any age; late-onset may be underrecognized.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case; anecdotal; no genetic characterization.

papers.title: Genetic Variants in LZTR1, MAP2K1 and RAF1: Insights into the Role of RAS-MAPK Pathway in Primary Lymphedema
papers.abstract: Retrospective analysis of 408 primary lymphedema patients identified five genetic variants in LZTR1, RAF1 and MAP2K1 genes. Four variants previously unreported, with molecular modeling supporting potential pathogenicity.
papers.what_happened: Italian cohort (n=408) identified 5 variants in LZTR1, MAP2K1, RAF1 in non-syndromic primary LE; 4 previously unreported.
papers.why_it_matters: First report of RAS-MAPK pathway variants in non-syndromic primary lymphedema; blurs syndromic/non-syndromic boundary.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective; computational pathogenicity only; single cohort; no functional validation.

papers.title: Intersection of two rare conditions: Clinical reflection on tuberous sclerosis combined with primary lymphedema
papers.abstract: Editorial discussing tuberous sclerosis complex combined with primary lymphedema, analyzing 16 previously reported pediatric cases.
papers.what_happened: Editorial reviews 16 pediatric TSC + primary lymphedema cases; discusses mTOR inhibitor relevance.
papers.why_it_matters: TSC-associated lymphatic manifestations may respond to sirolimus; mTOR-lymphatic connection.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Editorial; heterogeneous historical cases; no standardized outcomes.

papers.title: Fluid Distribution: Response to Intermittent Pneumatic Compression in People With and Without Primary Lymphedema
papers.abstract: Study measured fluid distribution before and after intermittent pneumatic compression in 15 primary lymphedema patients aged 11-40 years versus controls.
papers.what_happened: Prospective study (n=15, age 11-40) of IPC fluid redistribution in primary lymphedema vs controls.
papers.why_it_matters: IPC mechanism specifically in primary (not secondary) lymphedema; biomarkers of therapeutic response.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Small n; pre/post design; acute surrogate; pediatric and adult pooled.

papers.title: A severe equinovarus foot in a child with primary lymphedema
papers.abstract: Case report of severe equinovarus foot deformity in a child with primary lymphedema.
papers.what_happened: Equinovarus foot deformity as a rare musculoskeletal complication of pediatric primary lymphedema.
papers.why_it_matters: Awareness of orthopedic complications in pediatric primary lymphedema requiring multidisciplinary management.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case; no genetic characterization.

papers.title: Pregnancy-induced giant vulvar lymphangioma circumscriptum associated with primary lower limb lymphedema: a case report
papers.journal: Journal of the Egyptian Women's Dermatologic Society
papers.abstract: Case report of giant vulvar lymphangioma circumscriptum developing during pregnancy in a 23-year-old female with ipsilateral primary lymphedema.
papers.what_happened: Pregnancy-precipitated vulvar lymphangioma in a woman with underlying primary lower limb lymphedema.
papers.why_it_matters: Pregnancy as a triggering factor for lymphatic decompensation; obstetric counseling implications.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case; anecdotal; no genetic characterization.

papers.title: Lymphatic Reconstructive Surgery in Primary and Secondary Lymphedema: A Comparative Outcome Study
papers.abstract: Study of 48 limbs found VLNT significantly more effective than LVA for limb volume reduction in primary (but not secondary) lymphedema.
papers.what_happened: Retrospective study of 48 limbs: VLNT > LVA for volume reduction in primary LE; no difference in secondary LE.
papers.why_it_matters: Suggests VLNT may be preferentially superior in primary lymphedema if replicated; one of few studies separating primary vs secondary surgical outcomes.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective; 48 limbs is small; surrogate endpoint; obesity not controlled; LVA/VLNT universally lack RCT evidence.

papers.title: The value of nonenhanced magnetic resonance imaging in the grading of primary lower extremity lymphedema
papers.journal: Journal of Vascular Surgery: Venous and Lymphatic Disorders
papers.abstract: Retrospective study of 124 patients: nonenhanced MRI effectively grades primary lower extremity lymphedema using subcutaneous fat diameter measurements.
papers.what_happened: Nonenhanced MRI grades primary lower extremity lymphedema effectively in 124 patients.
papers.why_it_matters: Contrast-free MRI staging standardizes grading without radiation or invasive lymphoscintigraphy.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective single-center; external validation absent; no outcome linkage.

papers.title: Phenotype and genetic variation analysis of primary congenital lymphedema caused by FLT4 gene mutations in a fetus
papers.abstract: Retrospective study of three fetuses: FLT4 mutations including novel c.3284G>A; variable postnatal courses.
papers.what_happened: Three fetuses with congenital lymphedema; FLT4 mutations including novel c.3284G>A; variable postnatal outcomes.
papers.why_it_matters: Prenatal phenotyping of FLT4/VEGFR3 variants; variable postnatal courses important for family counseling.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Three fetuses only; novel variant lacks functional validation; fetal phenotype does not predict postnatal course.

papers.title: Lymphatic Embolization for Primary Genital Lymphorrhea and Chylous Reflux-Related Lower Limb Lymphedema
papers.journal: Journal of Vascular and Interventional Radiology
papers.abstract: Retrospective analysis of 11 patients: lymphatic embolization achieved 90% clinical success for genital lymphorrhea, 50% for leg lymphedema.
papers.what_happened: Lymphatic embolization in 11 primary genital lymphorrhea/chylous reflux patients: 90% genital success, 50% leg success.
papers.why_it_matters: Early evidence for minimally invasive option for primary genital lymphorrhea with limited alternatives.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Small n (11); single-arm retrospective; 50% leg success limits claims.

papers.title: Milroy's Disease With Chronic Lymphedema and Recurrent Bilateral Chylothorax
papers.journal: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine
papers.abstract: ATS 2025 abstract: Milroy's disease with chronic lymphedema and recurrent bilateral chylothorax.
papers.what_happened: ATS 2025 abstract: Milroy disease with chronic lymphedema and recurrent bilateral chylothorax.
papers.why_it_matters: Chylothorax as an extra-limb complication of Milroy disease to monitor for.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Abstract only; single case; no genetic confirmation in available text.

papers.title: RNA-sequencing unveils FLT4 splice site variants in variable congenital heart disease
papers.abstract: RNA-sequencing identified FLT4 splice site variants as a cause of variable congenital heart disease phenotypes.
papers.what_happened: FLT4 splice site variants identified in congenital heart disease; expands genotype-phenotype map beyond lymphedema.
papers.why_it_matters: Relevant to patients with FLT4 mutations presenting with cardiac-lymphatic overlap phenotypes.
papers.what_limits_confidence: CHD-focused; lymphedema is secondary consideration; translation to lymphedema practice indirect.

papers.title: The structured light scanner is a reliable, valid, and clinically feasible 3D laser scanner to assess leg volume in patients with leg lymphedema
papers.abstract: Study investigated reliability, concurrent validity, and clinical feasibility of a structured light scanner for measuring leg volume in lymphedema patients. Cross-sectional analysis of 33 patients (66 legs) showed the scanner demonstrated excellent reliability and strong correlation with circumference measurements and optoelectronic volumetry, with superior clinical feasibility compared to conventional methods.
papers.what_happened: A cross-sectional study of 33 lymphedema patients found a structured light scanner demonstrated excellent reliability and strong concurrent validity versus conventional leg volume measurement methods.
papers.why_it_matters: Better volumetry tools could reduce measurement burden and improve treatment-response monitoring in lymphedema clinical practice.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-center cross-sectional design with 33 patients; population included mixed lymphedema types with no primary-specific subgroup analysis.
key_findings: Structured light scanner showed excellent reliability and strong correlation with optoelectronic volumetry
Superior clinical feasibility vs conventional methods
n=33 patients, 66 legs, mixed lymphedema types

papers.title: Does Bariatric Surgery Improve Lymphedema? A Scoping Review
papers.abstract: Scoping review examining lymphatic disease burden in bariatric surgery populations and metabolic bariatric surgery impact on lymphedema. Review of 6 studies showed variable limb volume reductions; however, objective physiologic assessments frequently demonstrated persistent lymphatic dysfunction despite weight loss.
papers.what_happened: A scoping review of 6 studies found variable limb volume reductions after bariatric surgery in lymphedema patients, but objective physiologic assessments frequently showed persistent lymphatic dysfunction despite weight loss.
papers.why_it_matters: Patients with obesity and lymphedema may consider bariatric surgery hoping it resolves lymphedema; this review suggests lymphatic dysfunction often persists despite volume improvement.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Only 6 studies in evidence base; scoping (not systematic) review methodology; underlying studies likely dominated by obesity-related or secondary lymphedema rather than primary lymphedema specifically.
key_findings: Variable limb volume reductions after bariatric surgery in 6 studies
Persistent lymphatic dysfunction on physiologic testing despite weight loss
Authors conclude bariatric surgery is adjunct, not definitive treatment for lymphedema

papers.title: Magnetic resonance lymphangiography in severe primary lymphedema of the right hand
papers.abstract: Case presentation of 19-year-old with progressive right hand swelling. Magnetic resonance lymphangiography demonstrated stage 2b lymphedema with markedly impaired lymphatic function, extensive fibrotic changes, and hypertrophy of adipose tissue consistent with primary lymphedema, guiding decision against surgical intervention.
papers.what_happened: A case report described a 19-year-old with stage 2b primary lymphedema of the right hand confirmed by MR lymphangiography showing impaired lymphatic function and fibrotic changes, guiding a decision against surgical intervention.
papers.why_it_matters: Upper extremity primary lymphedema is rare and imaging documentation in young patients is sparse; the case illustrates MRL role in guiding management decisions.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case report with no generalizability; MR lymphangiography is already established for lymphatic assessment; no new clinical information beyond the individual case.
key_findings: MRL confirmed stage 2b primary lymphedema in right hand of 19-year-old
Fibrotic changes and adipose hypertrophy on imaging supported non-surgical management

papers.title: Emerging trends in artificial intelligence research in lymphedema: An evaluation in light of bibliometric and altmetric data
papers.abstract: Bibliometric and altmetric analysis of 43 artificial intelligence-related lymphedema articles (1975-2025). US and China led in output. General AI applications and risk prediction emerged as dominant themes, with moderate correlation between citations and online visibility.
papers.what_happened: A bibliometric and altmetric analysis of 43 AI-related lymphedema papers (1975-2025) found US and China leading in output, with general AI applications and risk prediction as dominant research themes.
papers.why_it_matters: Summarizes the current landscape of AI applications in lymphedema research and may guide future research prioritization.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Bibliometric analysis describes publication patterns only, not clinical utility; 43-paper corpus is small; primary lymphedema not distinguished from secondary.
key_findings: 43 AI-related lymphedema papers from 1975-2025
US and China lead in output
Risk prediction and general AI applications dominate research themes

papers.title: Interventions and platforms that direct lymphangiogenesis to restore physiological homeostasis and enhance immunoregulation
papers.abstract: Review of opportunities and obstacles for biomolecular pathway modulation, nanotechnology, and tissue engineering to promote or inhibit lymphangiogenesis, with applications in lymphedema, cancer metastasis, chronic wounds, and transplant rejection.
papers.what_happened: A review in NPJ Regenerative Medicine summarized current strategies for directing lymphangiogenesis using biomolecular pathway modulation, nanotechnology, and tissue engineering for applications in lymphedema and related conditions.
papers.why_it_matters: Comprehensive overview of the mechanistic landscape for lymphangiogenesis interventions, relevant to researchers developing primary lymphedema therapies targeting VEGF-C and related pathways.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Narrative review without systematic methodology; covers broad disease contexts beyond primary lymphedema; most strategies remain preclinical with historically poor translational record in lymphatic disease.
key_findings: Biomolecular, nanotechnology, and tissue engineering approaches for lymphangiogenesis reviewed
Both promotion and inhibition of lymphangiogenesis are relevant therapeutic contexts
Review covers lymphedema, cancer metastasis, chronic wounds, transplant rejection

papers.title: Molecular targeted treatment in infants with central conducting lymphatic anomalies
papers.abstract: Case series of infants with neonatal-onset central conducting lymphatic anomaly (CCLA) treated with mTOR and/or MEK inhibitors. Genetic testing identified pathogenic variants in four patients. MR lymphangiography revealed improved lymphatic flow on follow-up. Substantial clinical improvement occurred with no relapses during mean follow-up of 10.3 months.
papers.what_happened: A Dutch pediatric case series described infants with neonatal-onset CCLA who showed substantial clinical improvement after mTOR and/or MEK inhibitor treatment; pathogenic variants were identified in 4 patients.
papers.why_it_matters: mTOR and MEK inhibitors may offer targeted therapy for genetically confirmed CCLAs, rare but potentially fatal neonatal lymphatic malformations; supports a precision-medicine approach.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Uncontrolled case series; baseline-only design; mean follow-up of 10.3 months is short; CCLAs in neonates differ mechanistically from primary lymphedema in older patients; poor mTOR translational history in lymphatic disease.
key_findings: Substantial clinical improvement with mTOR and/or MEK inhibitors in neonatal CCLA
Pathogenic variants in 4 patients on genetic testing
MRL showed improved lymphatic flow on follow-up
No relapses at mean 10.3 months after therapy taper

papers.title: Molecular Characterization of Vascular Anomalies Tissues Guides Clinical Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Evaluated DNA from affected tissue of 58 patients with clinically diagnosed vascular anomalies using a custom 735-gene NGS panel. Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants identified in 47% of cases, with 61.5% detection rate for lymphatic malformations specifically. Two novel variants in LM tissue were found.
papers.what_happened: A 735-gene NGS panel applied to tissue biopsies from 58 vascular anomaly patients identified pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in 47% overall and 61.5% of lymphatic malformation cases.
papers.why_it_matters: Molecular characterization can identify targetable genetic variants in lymphatic malformations and guide precision treatment; 61.5% detection rate supports NGS in the diagnostic workup.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective single-center; requires invasive tissue biopsy; small subgroups within mixed vascular anomaly population; likely pathogenic classifications provisional without functional validation.
key_findings: 61.5% pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant detection rate in lymphatic malformations
47% overall detection across vascular anomaly types
Two novel variants in LM tissue
Custom 735-gene NGS panel on tissue samples

papers.title: Venolymphatic Malformation Presenting as a Low-Flow Vascular Anomaly: A Case Report
papers.abstract: A 15-year-old male presented with slow-growing right parotid swelling characteristic of venolymphatic malformation (VLM), a rare congenital disorder involving vascular and lymphatic systems. Multimodal imaging and image-guided sclerotherapy established diagnosis and provided effective minimally invasive treatment.
papers.what_happened: A case report described a 15-year-old with venolymphatic malformation presenting as right parotid swelling, managed successfully with multimodal imaging and image-guided sclerotherapy.
papers.why_it_matters: Illustrates diagnosis and minimally invasive management of a rare congenital lymphovascular malformation in an adolescent.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case report; VLMs are clinically heterogeneous; no follow-up duration or outcome quantification reported.
key_findings: VLM successfully treated with image-guided sclerotherapy
Multimodal imaging used for diagnosis of parotid VLM in adolescent

papers.title: Pathophysiological Changes in Primary Lymphedema: A Comprehensive Analysis of Histological and Molecular Alterations and Lymphatic Reconstruction Outcomes
papers.abstract: This monocentric case-control study investigated histological and molecular characteristics of primary lymphedema patients and microsurgical outcomes. Biopsies from affected and unaffected extremities of 15 patients undergoing lymphatic reconstructive surgery were compared with 8 healthy controls. Findings revealed significantly reduced cutaneous fibrosis and downregulation of CLDN5 and VEGFD expression in primary lymphedema patients. TJP1 expression was significantly decreased in affected but not unaffected sides. Microsurgical outcomes showed notable variability. The pathophysiological profile is characterized by unexpected extracellular matrix alterations and increased vascular permeability, both locally and systemically, suggesting a novel link between lymphatic dysfunction and fibrosis development.

claim_audit.comparator: healthy controls and unaffected contralateral limbs

papers.what_happened: A monocentric case-control study compared tissue biopsies from 15 primary lymphedema patients undergoing reconstructive surgery versus 8 healthy controls, finding unexpected reductions in cutaneous fibrosis and downregulation of tight junction proteins CLDN5, VEGFD, and TJP1 in affected limbs.
papers.why_it_matters: Direct molecular characterization of primary lymphedema tissue is rare; the finding of reduced (rather than increased) fibrosis and impaired endothelial barrier function challenges assumptions about primary lymphedema pathophysiology and may guide future therapeutic targets.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Very small sample (n=15 patients, n=8 controls); surgical selection bias — biopsies come from patients already undergoing reconstruction, not a representative primary lymphedema cohort; single-center; no genetic subtyping of enrolled patients.
key_findings: Reduced cutaneous fibrosis in primary lymphedema (unexpected — opposite of secondary LE)
Downregulation of CLDN5 and VEGFD in primary lymphedema tissue
TJP1 decreased in affected but not unaffected limbs — local not systemic effect
Variable microsurgical outcomes across n=15 patients
Suggests novel pathophysiology: impaired endothelial barrier rather than fibrotic obstruction

papers.title: Pediatric Extremity Vascular Malformations: Diagnosis, Referral, and Limb Management from a Pediatric Orthopedic Perspective
papers.abstract: Extremity vascular malformations in children and adolescents are congenital vascular developmental abnormalities that often present to pediatric orthopedic surgeons with pain, swelling, restricted motion, contracture, gait disturbance, limb asymmetry, and growth-related deformity. This review translates contemporary vascular anomaly classification into a practical orthopedic framework for diagnosis, referral, and longitudinal limb management. The most useful first step involves distinguishing low-flow from high-flow lesions and defining lesion depth, periarticular involvement, and syndromic overgrowth phenotype. Ultrasound serves as the first-line imaging modality for flow characterization, while magnetic resonance imaging defines extent and guides treatment planning.
papers.what_happened: A narrative review in Journal of Clinical Medicine translated contemporary vascular anomaly classification into a practical orthopedic management framework for pediatric extremity vascular malformations, including lymphatic malformations.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides a practical multi-specialty management framework for pediatric lymphatic malformations, which are developmental lymphatic anomalies in scope for this database.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Narrative review without systematic methodology; lymphatic malformations are one subtype among broader vascular anomalies; orthopedic perspective may not capture full clinical spectrum.
key_findings: Low-flow vs high-flow distinction is the key first diagnostic step
Ultrasound first-line; MRI defines extent for treatment planning
Syndromic overgrowth (CLOVES, PIK3CA spectrum) requires targeted workup
Orthopaedic management must address limb length discrepancy, joint deformity, and growth

papers.title: Endothelial von Hippel-Lindau gene deletion causes abnormal blood and lymphatic vasculature through ectopic activation of the HIF-CXCR4 axis
papers.abstract: The von Hippel-Lindau protein regulates cellular oxygen sensing by degrading hypoxia-inducible factors under normoxic conditions. Using a skin vasculature model, researchers investigated vascular development in mice with endothelial cell-specific Vhl deletion. Mutants exhibited abnormal vascular and lymphatic network formation and embryonic lethality. The deletion led to ectopic expression of chemokine receptor CXCR4 through HIF stabilization in endothelial cells. Treatment with AMD3100, a CXCR4 antagonist, partially restored vascular abnormalities caused by Vhl deletion. These findings identify the HIF-CXCR4 axis as a novel pathway controlling lymphatic vasculature development.
papers.what_happened: A preclinical mouse study found that endothelial-specific VHL deletion causes abnormal lymphatic vasculature development via HIF-stabilized ectopic CXCR4 expression, and that a CXCR4 antagonist (AMD3100) partially rescued the phenotype.
papers.why_it_matters: Identifies the HIF-CXCR4 signaling axis as a novel regulator of lymphatic vasculature development, providing a potential new mechanistic pathway relevant to developmental lymphatic anomalies and possibly primary lymphedema.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Entirely preclinical mouse model; VHL mutations in humans cause VHL syndrome (hemangioblastomas, clear-cell RCC) with lymphedema not as a primary feature; embryonic lethality in mutants limits extrapolation to lymphedema pathophysiology; lymphedema has a poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record.
key_findings: Endothelial VHL deletion causes abnormal blood and lymphatic vasculature in mouse
HIF stabilization leads to ectopic CXCR4 expression in endothelial cells
CXCR4 antagonist AMD3100 partially rescues vascular defects
Identifies HIF-CXCR4 axis as novel regulator of lymphatic development

papers.title: Disruption of the VEGFR3-HSPG2 interaction induces lymphatic reflux dysfunction and sepsis
papers.abstract: Preprint investigating the role of VEGFR3-HSPG2 protein interaction in lymphatic function. Disruption of this interaction in an animal model induces lymphatic reflux dysfunction and leads to sepsis, suggesting that HSPG2 is a critical binding partner for VEGFR3 in maintaining normal lymphatic valve and vessel function.
papers.what_happened: A preprint (bioRxiv, January 2026) reports that disruption of the VEGFR3-HSPG2 protein interaction in an animal model causes lymphatic reflux dysfunction and sepsis, identifying HSPG2 as a novel VEGFR3 binding partner.
papers.why_it_matters: VEGFR3/FLT4 loss-of-function mutations are the most common cause of Milroy disease; understanding VEGFR3 binding partners and regulation may reveal new therapeutic entry points for VEGFR3-mediated primary lymphedema.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Preprint — not yet peer-reviewed; item is 4 months old (published January 2026) and stale relative to this week's digest window; full abstract not available via search APIs; entirely preclinical with poor lymphedema translational track record.
key_findings: VEGFR3-HSPG2 interaction is required for normal lymphatic function in animal model
Disruption of this interaction causes lymphatic reflux and sepsis
HSPG2 identified as novel VEGFR3 binding partner
Implications for VEGFR3-dependent primary lymphedema (Milroy disease)

papers.title: Bleeding Diathesis in Hypotrichosis-Lymphedema-Telangiectasia Syndrome due to Decreased von Willebrand Factor
papers.journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics. Part A
papers.abstract: Hypotrichosis-lymphedema-telangiectasia syndrome (HLTS) is a congenital disorder caused by SOX18 gene mutations. A 10-year-old boy presented with aortic valve regurgitation, marbled skin, and iron-deficiency anemia from frequent mucosal bleeding. Hemostatic difficulties followed tooth extraction at age 5. Blood coagulation analysis revealed decreased platelet agglutination and reduced von Willebrand factor (vWF) levels. Whole-genome sequencing identified a heterozygous SOX18 pathogenic variant c.481C>T, p.Gln161Ter but no VWF gene mutations. Since SOX18 influences vWF expression in stem cells, decreased vWF may constitute an HLTS complication. vWF replacement therapy enabled safe dental procedures and stabilized hemoglobin levels.
papers.what_happened: A case report describes a 10-year-old boy with HLTS (SOX18 pathogenic variant c.481C>T, p.Gln161Ter) who had unexpectedly low von Willebrand factor levels causing recurrent mucosal bleeding and hemostatic difficulties; vWF replacement therapy enabled safe dental procedures.
papers.why_it_matters: HLTS is a primary lymphedema syndrome caused by SOX18 mutations; this is the first published case linking SOX18/HLTS to reduced vWF, with a mechanistic rationale (SOX18 regulates vWF expression in stem cells), suggesting pre-procedural hemostatic screening should be considered in HLTS patients.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case report — prevalence of vWF deficiency across the broader HLTS population is unknown; causal mechanism from SOX18 to reduced vWF in lymphatic endothelium is not directly validated in this case; n=1 with no comparison group.
key_findings: First reported association between HLTS (SOX18 mutation) and reduced von Willebrand factor
SOX18 c.481C>T, p.Gln161Ter — pathogenic variant with dominant-negative mechanism
No VWF gene mutations found — reduced vWF is secondary to SOX18 dysfunction
vWF replacement therapy successfully managed bleeding around dental procedures
Clinical implication: consider vWF assessment before elective procedures in HLTS patients

papers.title: Aquaporin-1 sustains lymphangiogenic responses in hyperosmotic inflammatory microenvironments
papers.abstract: Intestinal lymphatic vessels undergo continuous renewal to function in hyperosmolar inflammatory environments. Single-cell RNA-sequencing of murine small intestinal lymphatic endothelial cells found lacteal cells expressed high levels of aquaporin-1 (AQP1). AQP1 deletion reduced lacteal length and impaired lipid uptake on high-fat diets. AQP1 promoted lymphatic endothelial cell migration under hyperosmotic stress by preserving cytoskeletal and junctional remodeling. AQP1 was upregulated during inflammatory remodeling in lymphedema and lymphatic malformations but not embryonic lymphangiogenesis, linking lacteal regeneration to inflammatory lymphatic remodeling.
papers.what_happened: A J Exp Medicine study using mouse scRNA-seq and genetic deletion found that aquaporin-1 (AQP1) is required for lymphatic endothelial cell migration under hyperosmotic stress, and is upregulated in human lymphedema tissue and lymphatic malformations — but not during embryonic lymphangiogenesis.
papers.why_it_matters: AQP1 defines a novel, inflammation-specific lymphangiogenic program distinct from developmental lymphangiogenesis, providing a potential target for conditions where lymphatic regeneration is impaired — including lymphedema and lymphatic malformations (both in scope for primary LE research).
papers.what_limits_confidence: Primarily mouse model work; the human tissue finding (upregulation in lymphedema/LM) is associative and does not establish causation; gut-specific lacteal biology may not translate directly to peripheral lymphatic insufficiency in primary lymphedema; no therapeutic intervention studied.
key_findings: AQP1 highly expressed in intestinal lacteal lymphatic endothelial cells (scRNA-seq)
AQP1 deletion impairs lacteal length and dietary lipid uptake
AQP1 required for LEC migration under hyperosmotic stress via cytoskeletal/junctional remodeling
AQP1 upregulated in human lymphedema tissue and lymphatic malformations
Inflammation-specific lymphangiogenesis program distinct from embryonic development

papers.title: Long-term Comparative Effectiveness of Microsurgical Treatment Options for Lower Limb Lymphedema: Lymphovenous Anastomosis vs. Vascularized Lymph Node Transfer
papers.journal: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery
papers.abstract: This retrospective cohort study compared LVA (n=123) and VLNT (n=28) in 151 patients with lower limb lymphedema, minimum 1-year follow-up (2015-2023). LVA demonstrated rapid improvements within first three months; VLNT showed slower but steady effectiveness increase throughout the one-year follow-up, gradually narrowing the effectiveness gap. Two postoperative complications occurred in VLNT; none in LVA. LVA provides greater short-term improvements independent of anastomosis count; VLNT exhibits gradual longer-term improvements.

claim_audit.comparator: active control (LVA vs VLNT, no conservative arm)

papers.what_happened: A retrospective cohort study of 151 lower limb lymphedema patients found LVA produced faster short-term improvement than VLNT, while VLNT showed slower but progressive gains over 12 months, narrowing the effectiveness gap.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides comparative effectiveness data between the two major microsurgical lymphedema procedures — a relevant question for surgical planning, though the study is not designed to compare surgery vs. no surgery.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective design; unequal group sizes (n=123 LVA vs n=28 VLNT); one-year maximum follow-up in a chronic condition; no conservative management comparator; surrogate volume/effectiveness endpoint; lymphedema type not specified (likely predominantly secondary); obesity/BMI change not controlled.
key_findings: LVA: rapid effectiveness gains within first 3 months post-surgery
VLNT: slower improvement trajectory with ongoing gains through 12 months
VLNT gap vs LVA narrows over time — may converge beyond 12 months
Complication rate: 2/28 (7.1%) for VLNT, 0/123 for LVA
No RCT comparator — surgical outcomes caution applies (standard caveat for all LVA/VLNT studies)

papers.title: Lymph-interpositional flap transfer promotes lymphatic flow restoration: A rabbit hindlimb model supports the lymph axiality concept
papers.journal: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery
papers.abstract: Rabbit hindlimb study evaluating lymph-interpositional flap transfer (LIFT) for lymphatic reconstruction. The LIFT(+) group maintaining lymphatic alignment showed significantly reduced hindlimb volume at week 3 and higher lymphatic reconnection rates via ICG lymphography versus controls. RT-PCR demonstrated elevated VEGF-C, CD31, and podoplanin expression with reduced TGF-β levels, supporting the 'lymph axiality' concept that directional lymphatic alignment is critical for effective surgical reconstruction.
papers.what_happened: A rabbit hindlimb model demonstrated that lymph-interpositional flap transfer with maintained directional lymphatic alignment reduced limb volume more effectively and improved ICG lymphography reconnection rates versus unaligned controls.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides preclinical mechanistic support for the 'lymph axiality' principle in lymphatic surgical reconstruction, with upregulation of VEGF-C and reduction in TGF-β as proposed biological correlates.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Rabbit model with unknown translational validity to human primary or secondary lymphedema; 3-week assessment timepoint is very short for a chronic disease; lymphatic alignment is difficult to reproduce reliably in human surgery; lymphedema has a poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record.
key_findings: Directional lymphatic alignment in flap transfer reduces hindlimb volume at week 3
ICG lymphography showed higher reconnection rates in aligned (LIFT+) vs. unaligned group
VEGF-C and podoplanin elevated, TGF-β reduced in LIFT+ group
Supports 'lymph axiality' concept: directional alignment matters for surgical outcomes
Entirely preclinical — no human data

papers.title: The Omentum as a Lymphoid Tissue: Its Molecular Aspects and Application in a Murine Model
papers.abstract: Activated omental tissue in mice upregulates HIF-1α and Ang2 followed by increased FOXC2 and PROX1 expression. Culture supernatants showed elevated VEGF-C. When applied to a murine hindlimb lymphedema model, omental-conditioned supernatant reduced peak edema, accelerated resolution, and increased skin thickness and lymphatic vessel density. Histological findings revealed enhanced lymphangiogenesis with reduced macrophage infiltration.
papers.what_happened: A murine study found that activated omental tissue upregulates FOXC2 and PROX1 expression and secretes VEGF-C; omental-conditioned supernatant reduced peak edema and promoted lymphangiogenesis in a hindlimb lymphedema mouse model.
papers.why_it_matters: FOXC2 and PROX1 are primary lymphedema genes; their upregulation by omental activation suggests a potential biological basis for the omentum's use as a vascularized lymph node transfer substrate, and hints at a paracrine VEGF-C mechanism.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Mouse model only; conditioned supernatant application is not clinically equivalent to omentum transfer surgery; FOXC2/PROX1 upregulation is context-specific and does not correct underlying genetic mutations causing primary lymphedema; very short follow-up in chronic disease model.
key_findings: Omental activation induces HIF-1α → Ang2 → FOXC2 + PROX1 expression cascade
Activated omentum secretes elevated VEGF-C into culture supernatant
Omental-conditioned supernatant reduces peak edema in murine lymphedema model
Increased lymphatic vessel density and reduced macrophage infiltration in treated mice
FOXC2/PROX1 connection: primary lymphedema gene network activated by omental stimulation

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in lymphedema: A systematic review of diagnostic and clinical applications
papers.journal: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery
papers.abstract: Systematic review of 18 studies (8720 patients) examining AI applications in lymphedema diagnosis and monitoring. Machine learning models achieved AUCs to 0.89; deep learning models reached diagnostic accuracies to 98%. Volumetric measurement tools correlated strongly with gold-standard methods. Authors conclude current evidence remains preliminary and highlight the need for larger, prospective validation studies.
papers.what_happened: A systematic review of 18 AI/ML lymphedema studies (8720 patients) found deep learning models achieve diagnostic accuracies up to 98%, while noting current evidence remains preliminary and requires larger prospective validation.
papers.why_it_matters: AI tools for early detection and volumetric monitoring could reduce measurement burden in lymphedema management, though the review does not distinguish primary from secondary LE populations.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Likely dominated by secondary (BCRL) lymphedema studies; 'accuracy up to 98%' likely reflects best-case results in restricted test sets — not representative clinical performance; no primary LE-specific analysis; evidence characterised by authors themselves as preliminary.
key_findings: 18 studies, 8720 patients reviewed
Deep learning diagnostic accuracy up to 98% in test sets
ML models AUC up to 0.89 for detection/risk stratification
Volumetric AI tools correlate with gold-standard measurements
Authors: current evidence preliminary, prospective validation needed

papers.title: Is lymphedema an inflammatory disease?
papers.abstract: Editorial examining the inflammatory characteristics of lymphedema as a chronic progressive condition, addressing the relationship between lymphatic dysfunction and inflammatory mechanisms in both primary and secondary lymphedema.
papers.what_happened: A perspective editorial by Stéphane Vignes (a leading French lymphologist) poses and addresses the question of whether lymphedema should be classified as an inflammatory disease.
papers.why_it_matters: The inflammatory hypothesis has direct therapeutic implications — if lymphedema is driven by chronic inflammation, anti-inflammatory agents (ketoprofen, dupilumab, anti-TGF-β) may be more central to management; Vignes's perspective carries weight given his clinical expertise.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Editorial only — no original data, no systematic methods; framing as a question without a definitive answer; abstract/full text unavailable for detailed assessment.
key_findings: Expert editorial questioning classification of lymphedema as inflammatory disease
By Stéphane Vignes, leading French lymphology expert
Relevant to therapeutic targeting of inflammation in primary lymphedema
No original data — opinion/synthesis piece

papers.title: Tailored Personas for Self-Management in Home-Based Rehabilitation for Participants With Lower Limb Lymphedema: A Qualitative Study
papers.journal: International Journal of Nursing Studies Advances
papers.abstract: Qualitative content analysis of 24 participants with lower limb lymphedema identified five distinct self-management personas: proactive optimistic self-managers; moderate health literacy with fluctuating behaviors; low motivation with emotional disengagement; limited knowledge with constrained self-management; and high cooperation but excessive health anxiety. Semi-structured interviews informed persona development. Findings reveal substantial heterogeneity in behavioral patterns, providing a framework for tailored intervention strategies.
papers.what_happened: A qualitative study of 24 lower limb lymphedema patients identified five distinct self-management behavioral personas to inform tailored home-rehabilitation interventions.
papers.why_it_matters: Recognising patient heterogeneity in self-management behavior is relevant to designing effective lymphedema management programs, though the study does not distinguish primary from secondary lymphedema.
papers.what_limits_confidence: n=24; qualitative methodology; no primary LE-specific subgroup; limited transferability outside the study setting; persona framework not yet validated in intervention trials.
key_findings: Five self-management personas identified across 24 LL lymphedema patients
Heterogeneity in motivation, knowledge, and health anxiety
Framework for tailoring home-rehabilitation interventions
Lymphedema type not specified (primary vs secondary)

papers.title: Evaluation of Patient-Reported Outcomes in Over 10,000 patients Using Pneumatic Compression Therapy for Lower Extremity Lymphedema.
papers.journal: Journal of Vascular Surgery. Venous and Lymphatic Disorders
papers.abstract: Lymphedema management includes compression, manual drainage, and surgical options. While compression shows clinical effectiveness, adherence challenges and patient dissatisfaction can compromise outcomes. A 2024 survey of 10,543 patients evaluated satisfaction, usage patterns, and symptom changes with pneumatic compression devices. Results showed high satisfaction improving with frequency of use; daily users reported the greatest benefit in swelling reduction (58%), heaviness relief (34%), and pain improvement (25%). Outcomes remained consistent between 45- and 90-day assessments.
papers.novelty_assessment: Fresh paper published June 2, 2026 — within W23 scan window
key_findings: High patient satisfaction with pneumatic compression devices in 10,543 LE patients
Daily use associated with greatest benefit: swelling -58%, heaviness -34%, pain -25% (self-reported)
Symptom improvement stable between 45 and 90-day assessments
papers.clinical_implications: Adherence counseling for daily pneumatic compression use may improve patient-reported outcomes; results are associative and require controlled validation.

claim_audit.conflicts_of_interest: Device manufacturer involvement not stated; vascular surgery group (Labropoulos, Stony Brook)

papers.what_happened: A retrospective survey of 10,543 lower extremity lymphedema patients found high satisfaction with pneumatic compression devices, with daily users reporting the greatest self-reported symptom improvement at 45 and 90 days.
papers.why_it_matters: Large-scale patient-reported outcome data for pneumatic compression are uncommon; the frequency-benefit association reinforces adherence counseling, which is a recognized management challenge in primary and secondary lymphedema.
papers.what_limits_confidence: No objective lymphedema measurements, no control group, selection bias toward adherent survey completers, and a mixed primary/secondary population without subgroup data limit causal inference.

papers.title: Safety Profile of Sclerosing Agents in the Management of Low-Flow Vascular Malformations of the Head and Neck—A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: Systematic review of 64 studies (2508 patients, 5193 sessions) examining safety profiles of sclerosing agents for head and neck low-flow vascular malformations. Overall complication rate was 11.2% per session (8.8% minor local events). Bleomycin showed a 13.5% complication rate. Polidocanol and doxycycline demonstrated superior safety profiles with no major complications documented. Ethanol was associated with higher rates of major complications.
papers.what_happened: A systematic review of 64 studies (2508 patients, 5193 sessions) found an 11.2% overall per-session complication rate for head and neck low-flow vascular malformation sclerotherapy; doxycycline and polidocanol had the best safety profiles while ethanol carried the highest major complication risk.
papers.why_it_matters: Lymphatic malformations (developmental lymphatic anomalies, in scope) are a primary indication for doxycycline sclerotherapy; this SR provides the largest published safety dataset for H&N sclerotherapy across VM types including LMs, informing procedural risk counseling for patients with congenital lymphatic anomalies.
papers.what_limits_confidence: The population is mixed VM types (predominantly venous malformations, with LMs as an unquantified subset); LM-specific safety data is not isolated from the aggregate results; component studies are mostly retrospective case series with heterogeneous methodology; findings are restricted to the head and neck anatomical region and may not generalise to limb or truncal LMs.
key_findings: 11.2% overall complication rate per sclerotherapy session for H&N low-flow VMs
Doxycycline and polidocanol: no major complications documented across the review
Bleomycin: 13.5% complication rate (minor and major combined)
Ethanol: highest major complication risk among agents reviewed
Minor local events dominate (8.8% of sessions); major events uncommon

papers.title: GLP-1 Receptors Are Enriched in the Lymphatic Endothelium and Their Pharmacological Activation With Semaglutide Improves the Pumping Capacity of Lymphatic Vessels.
papers.abstract: GLP-1 receptors were detected exclusively in lymphatic endothelial cells by scRNA-seq and confocal microscopy. The GLP-1R agonist semaglutide produced robust vasodilation and increased the pumping capacity of isolated collecting lymphatics from WT, diet-induced obese, and hypercholesterolemic ApoE KO mice, mediated in part by nitric oxide and potential NaV-channel interaction.
key_findings: Glp1r expression localized exclusively to lymphatic endothelial cells
Semaglutide increased collecting-lymphatic pumping capacity ex vivo via NO-dependent vasodilation
papers.what_happened: In mouse tissue, GLP-1 receptors were found exclusively on lymphatic endothelial cells, and semaglutide increased the ex vivo pumping capacity of collecting lymphatics through nitric-oxide-dependent vasodilation.
papers.why_it_matters: GLP-1 agonists are in widespread clinical use; a direct, receptor-level effect on lymphatic contractility is a plausible mechanistic lead relevant to lymphatic function across lymphedema types, including primary.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Entirely preclinical (isolated mouse vessels, surrogate contractility endpoint) with no primary-lymphedema model or human data, and the authors frame the indication around secondary lymphedema.

papers.title: Sirolimus Therapy and Dyslipidemia in Neonates and Infants: A Retrospective Cohort and Pharmacovigilance Analysis.
papers.abstract: Single-center retrospective cohort (Nagoya University Hospital, Oct 2018-Sep 2025, n=10, median age 44.5 days) plus VigiBase pharmacovigilance disproportionality analysis. Post-initiation, 100% developed hypertriglyceridemia and 90% hypercholesterolemia. In VigiBase (17,802 sirolimus reports), the dyslipidemia reporting signal was highest in infants (28 days-23 months), aROR 147.08 (95% CI 79.67-271.54).
key_findings: 100% hypertriglyceridemia and 90% hypercholesterolemia in 10 sirolimus-treated neonates/infants
VigiBase dyslipidemia reporting signal highest in infants (aROR 147)
papers.what_happened: In sirolimus-treated neonates/infants (n=10), all developed hypertriglyceridemia and 90% hypercholesterolemia, and a VigiBase analysis showed the strongest dyslipidemia reporting signal in infants (aROR 147).
papers.why_it_matters: Sirolimus is first-line for generalized lymphatic anomalies (a primary lymphatic disorder), so quantifying a frequent, monitorable metabolic toxicity in the youngest patients is directly useful for safety monitoring.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Small single-center cohort plus pharmacovigilance disproportionality (reporting bias, no true denominator), and the population spans mixed vascular/lymphatic anomalies rather than a defined primary-lymphedema subtype.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Sirolimus Therapy for Neonates With Generalized Lymphatic Anomalies With Fetal Hydrops.
papers.abstract: Abstract not available in PubMed. Title reports on the effectiveness of sirolimus therapy for neonates with generalized lymphatic anomalies (GLA) presenting with fetal hydrops.
key_findings: Reports sirolimus effectiveness in neonatal GLA with fetal hydrops (full data not retrievable)
papers.what_happened: A report describes the effectiveness of sirolimus in neonates with generalized lymphatic anomalies presenting with fetal hydrops (abstract not available).
papers.why_it_matters: GLA with fetal hydrops is a severe primary lymphatic disorder with no approved therapy, so any added clinical experience with sirolimus is relevant to a high-mortality population.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Abstract unavailable; the title-level claim of effectiveness almost certainly rests on a small uncontrolled case series, and the underlying event (Jan 2026) is not new this week.

papers.title: Sirolimus Treatment for Complex Fetal and Neonatal Vascular Anomalies: Emerging Evidence and Safety Considerations.
papers.abstract: Narrative review of emerging evidence and safety considerations for sirolimus treatment of complex fetal and neonatal vascular anomalies, including lymphatic anomalies.
key_findings: Narrative synthesis of sirolimus evidence and safety in fetal/neonatal vascular and lymphatic anomalies
papers.what_happened: A narrative review summarizes emerging evidence and safety considerations for sirolimus in complex fetal and neonatal vascular anomalies, including lymphatic anomalies.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides a current reference point for sirolimus use in developmental lymphatic anomalies, which overlap the primary-lymphedema spectrum.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Narrative review without systematic methodology; no new primary data and broad scope beyond lymphatic disease.

papers.title: Common cutaneous signs unmasking a severe hematological disorder: GATA2 deficiency.
papers.abstract: Case report of a 31-year-old woman with childhood-onset progressive primary lymphedema, diffuse treatment-resistant warts, and severe monocytopenia, found on genetic testing to have GATA2 deficiency.
key_findings: Childhood-onset primary lymphedema as a presenting sign of GATA2 deficiency with monocytopenia
papers.what_happened: A case report describes a 31-year-old woman whose childhood-onset primary lymphedema, resistant warts, and monocytopenia led to a diagnosis of GATA2 deficiency.
papers.why_it_matters: Reinforces that primary lymphedema can be the presenting feature of GATA2/Emberger-spectrum disease, a serious hematologic-immunologic disorder requiring surveillance.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case report with no new mechanistic or therapeutic data, and the underlying publication (Jan 2026) is not new this week.

papers.title: Microsurgical Treatment of Lower Extremity Lymphedema: A PEER Umbrella Systematic Review Supporting the American Venous Forum and the American Vein and Lymphatic Society Clinical Practice Guidelines on Management of Lymphedema.
papers.journal: Journal of Vascular Surgery. Venous and Lymphatic Disorders
papers.abstract: PEER umbrella systematic review synthesizing 26 systematic reviews (14 meta-analyses; no RCTs identified, 2010-2025) of microsurgical treatment/prevention of lower-extremity lymphedema (LVA, VLNT, immediate lymphatic reconstruction) to inform forthcoming AVF/AVLS clinical practice guidelines. Conclusions were driven by four moderate-quality treatment reviews and one high-quality prevention review meeting all critical AMSTAR-2 domains; findings synthesized qualitatively due to substantial primary-study overlap.
key_findings: 26 SRs / 14 meta-analyses, no RCTs found for lymphatic microsurgery
Conclusions driven by 4 moderate-quality treatment reviews + 1 high-quality prevention review
papers.what_happened: An umbrella systematic review of 26 prior reviews (14 meta-analyses; no RCTs) synthesizes LVA/VLNT/immediate-lymphatic-reconstruction evidence to inform forthcoming AVF/AVLS lower-extremity lymphedema guidelines.
papers.why_it_matters: It defines the current best-evidence basis for lymphatic microsurgery and will directly shape US clinical practice guidelines.
papers.what_limits_confidence: No RCTs exist and primary studies overlap heavily across reviews; the population is predominantly secondary lower-extremity lymphedema, so direct applicability to primary lymphedema is indirect and the longstanding surgical evidence gap persists.

papers.title: Non-image-guided injection of bleomycin to treat orbital-adnexal lymphatic malformations: Effect of lesion morphology and previous treatment on outcomes.
papers.abstract: Retrospective single-center study of non-image-guided intralesional bleomycin sclerotherapy in 51 patients with orbital-adnexal lymphatic malformations (microcystic 60%, macrocystic ~19%, mixed ~28%; mean age 27.5 y; minimum 1-year follow-up). Outcomes graded by clinical regression (excellent >75% to poor <25%).
key_findings: Retrospective series (n=51) of intralesional bleomycin for orbital-adnexal lymphatic malformations
papers.what_happened: A retrospective single-center series (n=51) reports regression outcomes of non-image-guided intralesional bleomycin for orbital-adnexal lymphatic malformations.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds sclerotherapy outcome data for a developmental lymphatic malformation subtype within the broader lymphatic-anomaly spectrum.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective, single-arm, with a subjective clinical-regression endpoint and a narrow anatomical site not generalizable to limb lymphedema.

papers.title: Extensive Cervicofacial Lymphatic Malformation With Hemorrhagic Component in a Neonate: Airway and Anesthetic Challenges in Surgical Management.
papers.abstract: Case report of a full-term neonate with an extensive hemorrhagic cervicofacial macro/microcystic lymphatic malformation causing airway obstruction, managed with intubation, partial debulking, and tracheostomy.
key_findings: Airway-focused management of a hemorrhagic neonatal cervicofacial lymphatic malformation
papers.what_happened: A case report describes airway control, partial debulking, and tracheostomy for a neonate with an extensive hemorrhagic cervicofacial lymphatic malformation.
papers.why_it_matters: Documents acute management of a severe developmental lymphatic malformation within the lymphatic-anomaly spectrum.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case focused on anesthetic/airway management with no lymphatic-biology or durable-outcome data.

papers.title: Recurrent pediatric vesical lymphangioma: The first case report of early relapse after transurethral resection and successful endoscopic management.
papers.abstract: Case report of a 10-year-old girl with bladder lymphangioma (dilated lymphatic channels without atypia) that recurred 2 months after complete transurethral resection and was managed by deeper re-resection, with no relapse at 12 months.
key_findings: First report of early recurrence of pediatric bladder lymphangioma after TUR, managed with deeper re-resection
papers.what_happened: A case report describes early recurrence of a pediatric bladder lymphangioma after transurethral resection, successfully managed with deeper endoscopic re-resection.
papers.why_it_matters: Notes recurrence behavior of a rare developmental lymphatic malformation subtype.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case at a rare anatomical site with no generalizable implications for primary limb lymphedema.

papers.title: Lymphaticovenous Anastomosis Reduces Pain in Selected Patients with Lower Limb Lymphedema.
papers.journal: Journal of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery
papers.abstract: Retrospective study of 14 patients (25 limbs) with lower limb lymphedema and pain who underwent lymphaticovenous anastomosis (LVA). Mean pre-op VAS 3.1 improved to 2.9 post-op (p=0.23, not significant); 35.7% had pain reduction, 42.9% no change, 21.4% worsening. Limb circumference fell 205.5->200.5 cm (p<0.01). Pain improvement correlated with circumference change (r=0.42) and post-op weight loss (r=0.49). Greater pain reduction in 'sharp'/'throbbing' pain; all worsening cases described 'heaviness'. Mean follow-up 268 days.
key_findings: Primary pain endpoint was not significant: mean VAS 3.1->2.9 (p=0.23); only 35.7% improved while 21.4% worsened.
Pain improvement correlated with post-operative weight loss (r=0.49) and limb circumference reduction (r=0.42), raising confounding.
Pain subtype mattered: 'sharp'/'throbbing' pain responded; 'heaviness' did not and tended to worsen.
papers.what_happened: A small retrospective single-arm study (n=14, 25 limbs) found that LVA did not significantly reduce average pain (VAS 3.1->2.9, p=0.23) in lower limb lymphedema of unspecified etiology, though a 'sharp/throbbing' pain subgroup improved.
papers.why_it_matters: Pain is a patient-important outcome, and the data offer a calibrated, mostly-null picture of LVA-for-pain that tempers the optimistic title.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective, n=14, no control arm, the primary pain endpoint was non-significant, etiology (primary vs secondary) is unspecified, and pain improvement was confounded by concurrent weight loss and volume reduction.

papers.title: (23)Na-MRI Measures Tissue Sodium in Human Leg Lymphedema.
papers.abstract: There are few objective tools to quantify lymphatic disease changes in anatomy and physiology of affected tissues. Tissue sodium could be a relevant physiological indicator of lymphatic disease, but its role in human lymphatic physiology has not been well characterized due to a lack of imaging methods to observe sodium and lymphatics together. A prospective, cross-sectional observational clinical trial enrolled participants with lower extremity lymphedema (LEL) and controls without lymphedema, using sodium-23 MRI ((23)Na-MRI) alongside magnetic resonance lymphangiography to measure tissue sodium content (TSC) and subcutaneous adipose tissue.
key_findings: Used sodium-23 MRI to quantify tissue sodium content in lower-extremity lymphedema vs non-lymphedema controls, a novel objective imaging biomarker.
Positioned tissue sodium content as a candidate physiological indicator of lymphatic disease, paired with MR lymphangiography.
Cross-sectional observational design with controls; no functional or longitudinal outcome reported.
papers.what_happened: A prospective cross-sectional observational study used sodium-23 MRI to quantify tissue sodium content in the legs of participants with lower-extremity lymphedema versus controls without lymphedema.
papers.why_it_matters: Objective quantitative biomarkers of lymphatic tissue change are scarce, and sodium MRI could offer a non-invasive physiological readout potentially applicable across lymphedema subtypes including primary disease.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Small cross-sectional observational design with a surrogate imaging endpoint, no functional or clinical outcome, and the lymphedema etiology (primary vs secondary) is not specified.

papers.title: Rethinking Early-Stage Lymphedema: Severe Fat Accumulation Despite Early Lymphoscintigraphy Findings.
papers.abstract: (No abstract available on PubMed.) Article reports that severe subcutaneous fat accumulation can be present in early-stage lymphedema despite only mild/early lymphoscintigraphy findings, with implications for staging and choice between debulking and lymphovenous anastomosis. Keywords: debulking, early stage, fat-dominant lymphedema, lymphoscintigraphy, lymphovenous anastomosis.
key_findings: Reports severe fat accumulation in early-stage lymphedema despite only early/mild lymphoscintigraphic abnormalities, challenging fluid-predominant assumptions about early disease.
Raises the question of whether debulking may be warranted earlier than current staging implies, vs physiologic surgery (LVA).
No abstract or methods available on PubMed to assess design, sample size, or population.
papers.what_happened: A Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery article argues that severe subcutaneous fat accumulation can already be present in early-stage lymphedema despite only mild lymphoscintigraphic abnormalities.
papers.why_it_matters: If fat deposition begins earlier than ISL staging implies, it could affect the timing of debulking versus physiologic surgery (e.g., LVA) and challenges the assumption that early-stage disease is purely fluid-predominant.
papers.what_limits_confidence: No abstract or methods are available on PubMed to assess study design, sample size, or population (primary vs secondary), and fat-volume claims in lymphedema are confounded by obesity/BMI, which is not reported.

papers.title: Mechanoreceptor plexin D1 regulates lymphatic valve morphogenesis and lymphedema pathogenesis.
papers.abstract: Lymphatic valves are essential for maintaining tissue fluid homeostasis, and their dysfunction leads to lymphedema, a morbid and disfiguring disease without a cure. Mechanical forces due to lymph flow are required for proper lymphatic valve development, yet it remains unclear how lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs) sense and decode mechanical signals. In this study, we identify the cell guidance semaphorin receptor plexin D1 (PLXND1) as a lymphatic mechanosensor required for lymphatic valve morphogenesis. Conditional genetic ablation of Plxnd1 in LECs caused major defects in lymphatic valve development in 2 different lymphatic vascular beds. Mechanistically, PLXND1 acted as a mechanosensor within a lymphatic mechanocomplex, initiating distinct mechanical signals and activating the lymphatic valve transcriptional program through an unconventional pathway. Screening of patients with primary lymphedema identified PLXND1 missense variants, and functional analysis established 2 pathogenic variants that selectively disrupt the ligand versus mechanosensing functions of this receptor. Variants associated with lymphedema in members of the mechanocomplex disrupted its formation, underscoring the central role of this complex in lymphatic valve biology. Our work uncovers a mechanosensing mechanism guiding lymphatic valve development, and has profound implications for the understanding and t
key_findings: Conditional deletion of Plxnd1 in lymphatic endothelial cells caused major lymphatic valve development defects in two distinct vascular beds in mice.
PLXND1 is proposed to act as a mechanosensor within a lymphatic mechanocomplex that activates the valve transcriptional program.

Screening of patients with primary lymphedema identified PLXND1 missense variants; two were functionally characterised as pathogenic, separately disrupting ligand-binding versus mechanosensing functions.
Variants in other mechanocomplex members associated with lymphedema disrupted complex formation.
papers.what_happened: A mouse genetics and cell-biology study identified the semaphorin receptor plexin D1 (PLXND1) as a lymphatic endothelial mechanosensor required for lymphatic valve morphogenesis, and reported PLXND1 missense variants in a screen of patients with primary lymphedema, two of which were functionally characterised as pathogenic.
papers.why_it_matters: Lymphatic valve failure is a core mechanism in several forms of primary lymphedema, and a mechanosensing pathway with matching human variants nominates PLXND1 as a candidate gene worth adding to primary-lymphedema sequencing panels and as a potential mechanistic target.
papers.what_limits_confidence: The causal evidence is preclinical (conditional mouse knockouts and in vitro assays); the human component is variant-level functional work without reported cohort frequencies, segregation, or phenotype detail, and lymphatic biology has a poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record, so no therapeutic inference is justified yet.

papers.title: SHOC2 Is a Novel Cause of Central Conducting Lymphatic Anomaly.
papers.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
papers.abstract: Central conducting lymphatic anomaly (CCLA) is a devastating disorder where precision medicine can be lifesaving. Diagnosing CCLA is challenging due to its broad spectrum of symptoms, including nonimmune fetal hydrops, chylothorax, chylous ascites, or lymphedema. For that reason, genetic diagnosis is essential to uncover new genes and variants causing this debilitating disease. A patient with complex congenital heart disease presented with post-operative refractory chylothorax. Lymphatic imaging demonstrated abnormal intercostal lymphatic perfusion consistent with CCLA and suggestive of a RASopathy, a group of genetic disorders characterized by dysregulated RAS-MAPK signaling. Genetic testing showed a variant of uncertain significance (p.(Ala308Val)) in SHOC2, a scaffolding protein that regulates RAS-MAPK signaling but has not yet been described in CCLA. Trametinib, a MEK1/2 inhibitor, was trialed without improvement. A conversion/extension assay was used to evaluate pathogenicity of the VUS compared to a known pathogenic variant. Zebrafish transiently expressing the wild type human SHOC2 protein or SHOC2 p.(Ala308Val) protein in the developing lymphatic and venous endothelium were used to evaluate the effect on the vasculature. Western blot was used to explore the underlying molecular mechanisms. Major to minor axis ratio was significantly increased in developing embryos injec
key_findings: A patient with complex congenital heart disease and refractory post-operative chylothorax had lymphatic imaging consistent with central conducting lymphatic anomaly and a SHOC2 variant of uncertain significance, p.(Ala308Val).
Zebrafish expressing the variant in lymphovenous endothelium developed pericardial edema, caudal plexus cystic malformations and thoracic duct dilation, supporting pathogenicity.
Trametinib (MEK1/2 inhibitor) was trialled clinically without improvement.
Immunoblotting suggested the variant may act through non-canonical mTOR signalling rather than canonical RAS-MAPK dysregulation, consistent with the absent trametinib response.
papers.what_happened: A single-patient report combined with zebrafish functional modelling proposed SHOC2 p.(Ala308Val) as a novel cause of central conducting lymphatic anomaly, with molecular data suggesting non-canonical mTOR rather than RAS-MAPK signalling and no clinical response to trametinib.
papers.why_it_matters: It adds a candidate gene to CCLA diagnostic sequencing and provides a cautionary datapoint that a RASopathy-associated gene does not automatically predict benefit from MEK inhibition, which bears on targeted-therapy selection in complex lymphatic anomalies.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is n=1 with a variant of uncertain significance, no family segregation data, and functional support from transient zebrafish overexpression rather than a knock-in model, so gene-disease association remains provisional.

papers.title: Serum indocyanine green quantification enables objective assessment of lymphatic function.
papers.abstract: Secondary lymphedema is characterized by impaired lymphatic drainage, yet current diagnostic approaches rely on limb volume measurements and qualitative measures of lymphatic function. In this study, we tested the hypothesis that systemic uptake following intradermal injection of fluorescent tracers can serve as a quantitative biomarker of lymphatic transport. Using various preclinical models of lymphatic dysfunction, including genetic VEGFR3 haploinsufficiency, inducible lymphatic endothelial cell depletion, aging, and surgical lymphatic injury, we show that decreased serum concentrations of intradermally administered indocyanine green (ICG) correlate with indicators of impaired lymphatic function, including reduced lymphatic vessel density, diminished lymphatic pumping, and impaired dendritic cell migration. Together, these findings suggest that quantification of the serum concentrations of peripherally injected dyes selectively transported by the lymphatic system may be a useful means of assessing lymphatic function.
key_findings: Serum concentrations of intradermally injected indocyanine green were reduced across several preclinical models of lymphatic dysfunction.
Models included genetic VEGFR3 haploinsufficiency, inducible lymphatic endothelial cell depletion, aging, and surgical lymphatic injury.
Reduced serum ICG correlated with lower lymphatic vessel density, diminished lymphatic pumping and impaired dendritic cell migration.
papers.what_happened: A preclinical study reported that serum concentrations of intradermally injected indocyanine green fall in mouse models of lymphatic dysfunction, including VEGFR3 haploinsufficiency, and correlate with vessel density, pumping and dendritic cell migration.
papers.why_it_matters: The field lacks quantitative, operator-independent measures of lymphatic transport, and inclusion of a VEGFR3 haploinsufficient model makes this potentially relevant to Milroy-type primary lymphedema as well as acquired disease.
papers.what_limits_confidence: All data are from animal models with no human validation, the readout is a surrogate of transport rather than a clinical outcome, and the paper is framed around secondary lymphedema despite the genetic model included.

papers.title: Sirolimus for non-immune hydrops due to vascular and lymphatic anomalies in preterm neonates: an imaging-anchored response phenotype from a level IV NICU.
papers.journal: Journal of perinatology : official journal of the California Perinatal Association
key_findings: Reports an imaging-anchored response phenotype for sirolimus in preterm neonates with non-immune hydrops attributable to vascular and lymphatic anomalies, from a single level IV NICU.
No abstract or methods are available on PubMed, so cohort size, comparator and response definition cannot be verified.
