Responsiveness was assessed via Global Perceived Effect scores after 2 months, and separately after 1 month of intensive treatment. Reported excellent reliability (ICC = .94), good internal consistency (alpha = .86), and moderate convergent validity with SF-36 (r = -0.48 to -0.72).
key_findings: French Lymph-ICF-LL shows excellent test-retest reliability (ICC=.94), good internal consistency (alpha=.86), and moderate convergent validity with SF-36 in patients with stable lower limb lymphedema.
Instrument also demonstrated responsiveness to change after treatment, correlating with Global Perceived Effect scores.
papers.what_happened: A French translation of the Lymph-ICF-LL quality-of-life questionnaire for lower limb lymphedema was validated in a prospective observational cohort, showing excellent reliability and moderate convergent validity with SF-36.
papers.why_it_matters: A validated French-language instrument lets French-speaking clinics and trials measure lymphedema-specific quality of life consistently with the wider Lymph-ICF-LL literature.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is a psychometric validation study, not a treatment or mechanistic finding, the etiology mix of the lower-limb lymphedema cohort (primary vs. secondary) is not specified, and it has no bearing on clinical practice beyond outcome-measure selection.
papers.triage_note: deep_2026-W32_001: scope genuinely ambiguous from title/abstract; left as unknown/new for future review, not deep-synthesized this round

papers.title: Successful management of lymphangioma circumscriptum of the tongue with sirolimus monotherapy: a case report.
papers.abstract: Case report of a patient with lymphangioma circumscriptum of the tongue (a congenital lymphatic malformation causing macroglossia) treated entirely nonsurgically with 17 months of sirolimus (mTOR inhibitor) monotherapy, given that the lesion's extent made surgical resection impractical without excessive morbidity. Response was monitored with serial T2 MRI. Outcome: full resolution of symptoms, no treatment-related toxicity.
key_findings: Single case of tongue lymphangioma circumscriptum achieved full resolution after 17 months of sirolimus monotherapy, monitored by T2 MRI, with no reported toxicity.

Consistent with the existing evidence base showing mTOR inhibition (sirolimus) as an active treatment for congenital/developmental lymphatic anomalies (see existing finding mtor_mek_neonatal_lymphatic_anomalies).
papers.what_happened: A single case report describes full resolution of tongue lymphangioma circumscriptum after 17 months of sirolimus monotherapy, monitored by MRI, with no toxicity.
papers.why_it_matters: It adds one more supporting case to the existing signal that mTOR inhibition is an effective medical (non-surgical) option for congenital lymphatic malformations that are difficult to resect.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is an n=1 case report with no control and no long-term follow-up beyond the treatment course, so it cannot establish efficacy on its own and only reinforces an already-documented mechanism rather than adding new evidence weight.

papers.title: Yellow Nail Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Narrative review of Yellow Nail Syndrome (YNS), a rare disorder defined by a triad of yellow nail discoloration, lymphedema, and respiratory tract disease (only two of three signs required for diagnosis). Discusses a hypothesized paraneoplastic/malignancy association, and notes management options: oral vitamin E for nail changes, serial thoracentesis for pleural effusions, and compression garments/bandaging for the lymphedema component.
key_findings: General narrative review of Yellow Nail Syndrome diagnostic triad and symptomatic management; no new primary data presented.
Notes a hypothesized association between YNS and malignancy, suggesting a possible paraneoplastic mechanism in some cases rather than a purely congenital/hereditary lymphatic defect.
papers.what_happened: A narrative dermatology review summarizes Yellow Nail Syndrome, a triad disorder that includes lymphedema, its hypothesized paraneoplastic association, and standard symptomatic management.
papers.why_it_matters: YNS is one of the recognized syndromes presenting with lymphedema and is useful background for differential diagnosis, but the review itself introduces no new evidence.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is a narrative (non-systematic) review with no new data, and the paper itself raises a paraneoplastic/malignancy-associated etiology for many YNS cases, meaning much of the underlying population this review draws on may not be genetic/primary lymphedema at all — kept as 'unknown' scope rather than 'primary' for that reason.

papers.title: Intestinal ultrasound in primary intestinal lymphangiectasia (Waldmann's disease): a PRISMA-ScR scoping review with an illustrative adult case.
papers.abstract: PRISMA-ScR scoping review of transabdominal B-mode intestinal ultrasound (IUS) findings in primary intestinal lymphangiectasia (PIL; Waldmann's disease), a rare protein-losing enteropathy caused by dilated intestinal lacteals leaking chyle into the gut lumen. Fifteen primary studies (1986-2026, nine paediatric, six adult) were synthesized, identifying a consistent sonographic signature: diffuse hypoechoic small-bowel-wall thickening with preserved stratification, dilated fluid-filled loops, oedematous mesentery, and characteristically absent mesenteric lymphadenopathy. Diagnostic accuracy as a screening tool was evaluated in only one small study (n=20, accuracy 80%). The review illustrates the signature with an anecdotal single-observation case in a 42-year-old woman with Hennekam syndrome.
key_findings: Scoping review of 15 studies describes a reproducible B-mode intestinal ultrasound signature for primary intestinal lymphangiectasia, a rare congenital lymphatic disorder distinct from limb lymphedema.
Diagnostic accuracy of ultrasound as a screening tool is supported by only one small study (n=20); most included studies are case reports/series rather than validation cohorts.

Illustrative case involves a patient with Hennekam syndrome, one of the primary lymphedema-associated genetic syndromes in scope, but the review's focus is GI diagnostic imaging technique, not lymphedema treatment or genetics.
papers.what_happened: A scoping review synthesizes 15 studies on intestinal ultrasound findings in primary intestinal lymphangiectasia (Waldmann's disease), a rare congenital lymphatic-leak disorder, illustrated with a case in a patient with Hennekam syndrome.
papers.why_it_matters: Waldmann's disease and Hennekam syndrome sit within the primary/congenital lymphatic disorder spectrum, and a non-invasive ultrasound signature could aid diagnosis without lymphoscintigraphy, but this is a diagnostic-imaging review, not a lymphedema treatment or genetics study.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Diagnostic accuracy as a screening tool rests on a single small study (n=20), most underlying evidence is case reports/series rather than controlled validation, and the paper's scope (GI ultrasound technique) is only tangentially about lymphedema — kept as 'unknown' lymphedema_type given the Hennekam-syndrome link rather than tagged 'primary'.

papers.title: What is the recommended compression pressure for different clinical indications?
papers.abstract: Compression pressure is the key factor determining effectiveness in compression therapy for venous and lymphatic disorders. Despite its clinical importance, few studies report the actual applied pressure, and national standards for compression classes differ. This review aims to identify the optimal compression pressure at different stages of venous disease. A literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (January 1980-October 2025).
papers.what_happened: A narrative review in Phlebology synthesizes published evidence on recommended compression pressure across venous and lymphatic clinical indications, without new primary data.
papers.why_it_matters: Compression pressure standardization is practically relevant to lymphedema management, but the review is not specific to primary lymphedema and covers venous disease broadly.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is a narrative synthesis rather than a primary study, and it does not isolate findings for primary (genetic/hereditary) lymphedema populations.

papers.title: Impact of Lymphedema Duration on Lymphatic Vessel Quality and Outcomes after Super-microsurgical Lymphaticovenous Anastomosis
papers.what_happened: A paper ahead-of-print in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery reports on how lymphedema duration relates to lymphatic vessel quality and outcomes after super-microsurgical lymphaticovenous anastomosis (LVA); no abstract is yet indexed in PubMed.
papers.why_it_matters: LVA timing relative to disease duration is a practical surgical-planning question, but this journal's LVA literature is dominated by secondary (BCRL) cases, so relevance to primary lymphedema cannot be confirmed yet.
papers.what_limits_confidence: No abstract or methods are currently available; the population (primary vs. secondary lymphedema) cannot be confirmed, and LVA outcome studies are almost universally single-arm and retrospective (surgical evidence gap).

papers.title: Reply: Impact of Lymphedema Duration on Lymphatic Vessel Quality and Outcomes after Super-microsurgical Lymphaticovenous Anastomosis
papers.what_happened: A reply/correspondence letter responding to the companion LVA-duration paper (pm_41434454) was indexed; no new data are presented.
papers.why_it_matters: Editorial correspondence of this kind rarely changes clinical or research decisions on its own.
papers.what_limits_confidence: No abstract or data are available; this is an editorial exchange, not a new study.

papers.title: Correction: High-frequency ultrasound combined with microbubbles for preoperative lymphatic mapping for lymphedema with a non-linear pattern in indocyanine green lymphography
papers.what_happened: A publisher correction notice was issued for an earlier European Radiology paper on high-frequency ultrasound plus microbubbles for preoperative lymphatic mapping in lymphedema with non-linear ICG lymphography patterns.
papers.why_it_matters: This is a metadata correction to previously published work, not new scientific data.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is a publisher correction notice; the underlying original study's population and findings are not reassessed here.

papers.title: Tailored Charles' procedure and vascularized lymph node transfer for advanced stage Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome.
papers.abstract: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome (KTS) is primarily managed for vascular and soft-tissue abnormalities, while treatment of associated lymphedema remains poorly described. This study outlines a protocol combining a modified Charles' procedure and vascularized lymph node transfer (VLNT) for advanced lower-extremity lymphedema in KTS. KTS patients with ISL stage III lower-limb lymphedema treated between 1999 and 2018 were retrospectively reviewed.
papers.what_happened: A retrospective, single-arm case series describes a combined modified Charles' procedure and vascularized lymph node transfer technique for advanced (ISL stage III) lower-limb lymphedema in Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome patients treated over a 19-year span (1999-2018).
papers.why_it_matters: Offers a described surgical protocol for a rare, difficult-to-treat congenital lymphatic-malformation population where published lymphedema-specific outcome data is scarce.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-arm retrospective series spanning two decades with no comparator arm or standardized outcome measures, so the magnitude and durability of benefit cannot be established from this design; surgical-outcomes evidence gap applies as usual.

papers.title: Updates on Lymphatic Malformations: Medical Therapies, Sclerotherapy, and Surgery.
papers.abstract: Lymphatic malformations represent a diverse group of congenital lymphatic disorders whose management has evolved with the advent of molecularly targeted therapies. Recognition of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway as a key driver of pathogenesis has transformed treatment, with sirolimus and alpelisib now complementing traditional procedural options. Successful management demands multidisciplinary collaboration, integrating medical, interventional, and surgical involvement and expertise.
papers.what_happened: A narrative review summarizes current medical (sirolimus, alpelisib), sclerotherapy, and surgical management options for lymphatic malformations.
papers.why_it_matters: Consolidates the shift toward molecularly-targeted PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway therapy for lymphatic malformations for clinicians and pipeline watchers tracking the field.
papers.what_limits_confidence: A narrative review presents no new primary data and reflects the authors' synthesis rather than a systematic evidence appraisal.

papers.title: Significant clinical, functional and radiological response with sirolimus in refractory complex orbital venolymphatic malformation.
papers.abstract: Orbital venolymphatic malformations (OVLM) are rare congenital vascular anomalies that may cause progressive proptosis, visual loss, facial disfigurement and marked psychosocial burden. We describe a school-aged child with a right eye refractory extensive orbital venolymphatic malformation leading to marked visual impairment and disfigurement despite multiple prior treatments, who showed significant clinical, functional and radiological response to sirolimus.
papers.what_happened: A single case report describes clinical, functional, and radiological improvement with sirolimus in a child with a treatment-refractory orbital venolymphatic malformation.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds one more anecdotal data point to the growing off-label use of sirolimus for complex vascular-lymphatic malformations refractory to conventional therapy, reinforcing the existing mTOR/MEK-inhibitor signal in this space.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-patient case report with no control and no standardized outcome measure; response in one child does not establish efficacy or predict response in others.

papers.title: Binding of RAS to PI3Kα regulates developmental and KRASG12D-induced lymphangiogenesis.
papers.abstract: Complex lymphatic anomalies (CLAs) are characterized by abnormal development of lymphatic vessels and can be caused by somatic activating mutations in KRAS, which stimulate MAPK and PI3K signaling. While KRAS/MAPK signaling is known to play a critical role in CLA pathogenesis, the contribution of KRAS/PI3Kalpha signaling remains unclear. Using mice carrying missense mutations in the RAS-binding domain of PI3Kalpha, this study shows RAS-PI3Kalpha binding contributes to developmental and KRASG12D-induced lymphangiogenesis.
papers.what_happened: A mouse genetic study finds that RAS binding to PI3Kalpha contributes to developmental and KRASG12D-driven lymphangiogenesis, implicating a RAS-PI3K axis alongside the established RAS-MAPK pathway in complex lymphatic anomalies.
papers.why_it_matters: Complex lymphatic anomalies are increasingly treated with MEK inhibitors on the premise that RAS-MAPK signaling drives disease; this preclinical finding suggests RAS-PI3K signaling may also contribute, relevant to explaining variable MEK-inhibitor response and to exploring alternative or combination targets. Extends the existing mTOR/MEK-in-neonatal-lymphatic-anomalies signal alongside the prior SHOC2 non-canonical-mTOR finding.
papers.what_limits_confidence: A mouse genetic model only; lymphatic disease has a poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record, and no human tissue or clinical correlation is presented.

papers.title: Prenatal diagnosis of congenital lymphatic malformation in an atypical location.
papers.what_happened: A case report describes prenatal diagnosis of a congenital lymphatic malformation in an atypical anatomic location; PubMed has no indexed abstract for this record.
papers.why_it_matters: Minimal on its own — a single case report; without an abstract, no assessment of clinical significance is possible from available metadata.
papers.what_limits_confidence: No abstract is indexed on PubMed; full-text review would be required before drawing any conclusion, and this is a single case report regardless.

papers.title: CXCL12/CXCR4 Governs Lymphatic Valve Formation Through Flow Dependent AKT/FOXO1/FOXC2 Activation.
papers.abstract: Lymphatic valves are specialized structures within lymphatic vessels that ensure unidirectional lymph transport. Defective lymphatic valve formation is associated with lymphedema. This study reports that CXCL12/CXCR4 signaling, acting through flow-dependent AKT/FOXO1/FOXC2 activation, governs lymphatic valve formation in mice.
papers.what_happened: An unreviewed bioRxiv preprint reports that CXCL12/CXCR4 signaling, acting through flow-dependent AKT/FOXO1/FOXC2 activation, governs lymphatic valve formation in mice.
papers.why_it_matters: Lymphatic valve defects are a proximate mechanism in FOXC2-linked lymphedema-distichiasis, so identifying an upstream signaling axis converging on FOXC2 could eventually point to new mechanistic or therapeutic targets.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is an unreviewed preprint (not yet peer-reviewed) in a mouse model; lymphatic-biology preclinical findings have historically translated poorly to human therapy, and no human primary-lymphedema data is presented.

papers.title: Validity, responsiveness, reliability and measurement error of imaging modalities for soft tissue oedema measurements: A systematic review and best-evidence synthesis.
papers.abstract: Effective lymphoedema management depends on early detection and treatment, emphasizing the need for measurement instruments with strong clinimetric properties. This systematic review aimed to identify and evaluate the measurement properties of imaging modalities used to assess soft tissue oedema, searching Embase, Medline, Web of Science, and CINAHL from inception to December 2, 2025.
papers.what_happened: A systematic review and best-evidence synthesis evaluates the reliability, validity, and responsiveness of imaging modalities used to measure soft-tissue oedema.
papers.why_it_matters: Better characterizes which imaging-based measurement tools have adequate clinimetric properties for tracking lymphedema, informing outcome-measure selection for future studies.
papers.what_limits_confidence: A methods/measurement review, not a treatment-outcome study; does not itself change clinical management and covers oedema broadly rather than primary lymphedema specifically.

papers.title: Multidimensional outcomes of initial treatment strategies for pediatric head and neck lymphatic malformations.
papers.abstract: This retrospective cohort study compares real-world initial treatment strategies for pediatric head and neck lymphatic malformations using a multidimensional outcome framework distinguishing complete radiological response, objective lesion response, progression control, and treatment burden, examining how lesion complexity influences treatment selection and outcomes at a tertiary referral center.
papers.what_happened: A retrospective single-center cohort study compares real-world initial treatment strategies for pediatric head-and-neck lymphatic malformations using a multidimensional outcome framework.
papers.why_it_matters: Provides comparative real-world outcome data across treatment strategies for a rare congenital anomaly where randomized evidence is essentially absent.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective single-center design without randomization; treatment selection is likely confounded by lesion complexity and clinician preference rather than by chance.

papers.title: NRAS mutation in a central conducting lymphatic anomaly and PPFIBP1::ROS1 fusion in a Gorham-Stout disease patient.
papers.abstract: Lymphatic malformations can lead to severe clinical complications. While genomic alterations have been identified in lymphatic malformations, the genomic landscape of complex lymphatic malformations remains poorly defined due to their rarity. This study reports an NRAS p.Q61R mutation in a central conducting lymphatic anomaly (CCLA) and a PPFIBP1::ROS1 fusion in a Gorham-Stout disease (GSD) patient, both described for the first time in their respective subtypes.
papers.what_happened: Two case reports describe novel genomic drivers in complex lymphatic anomalies: an NRAS p.Q61R mutation in a central conducting lymphatic anomaly, and a PPFIBP1::ROS1 gene fusion in Gorham-Stout disease, each reported for the first time in its subtype.
papers.why_it_matters: Expands the known genomic landscape of complex lymphatic anomalies and, in the ROS1-fusion case, raises the possibility of testing an existing class of targeted inhibitors, though no treatment response is reported here.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-patient genomic findings with no functional validation or reported treatment response; identifying a fusion or mutation does not by itself establish that it drives disease or that a matched inhibitor would help.

papers.title: A Systematic Review on Imaging and Diagnostic Modalities for the Detection, Evaluation, and Surgical Planning of Upper and Lower Extremity Lymphedema.
papers.journal: Journal of Vascular Surgery: Venous and Lymphatic Disorders
papers.abstract: This systematic review, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, reviews imaging and diagnostic modalities for their roles in diagnosing upper and lower extremity lymphedema, detecting subclinical disease through prospective surveillance, providing anatomical assessment of the lymphatic system, and guiding surgical treatment planning. Search included PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Scopus from January 2010 to April 2026.
papers.what_happened: A PRISMA systematic review evaluates imaging and diagnostic modalities used for diagnosis, subclinical surveillance, anatomical assessment, and surgical planning in upper and lower extremity lymphedema.
papers.why_it_matters: Consolidates the evidence base on which imaging tools serve which diagnostic or surgical-planning purpose, useful for standardizing lymphedema workup.
papers.what_limits_confidence: A systematic review of existing literature, not new primary data; included studies span both primary and secondary lymphedema without disaggregating findings by etiology.

papers.title: An Adult Presentation of KIF11-Related MCLID Syndrome: Case Report and 40-Year Follow-Up.
papers.journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A
papers.abstract: Pathogenic variants in KIF11 are linked to autosomal dominant syndromes with microcephaly, chorioretinopathy, lymphedema, and intellectual disability (MCLID), though adult presentations remain underreported. We report a 42-year-old female presenting with a de novo single-amino acid in-frame deletion in the KIF11 gene (c.1294_1296del; p.Glu432del), who exhibited severe intellectual disability, microcephaly, hypotonia, seizures, and self-injurious behavior. There was evidence of developmental delays, ophthalmologic findings, and impairments in speech and adaptive functioning in her clinical history. Trio whole exome sequencing identified a diagnostic pathogenic variant in KIF11 and a maternally inherited SCN3A variant of uncertain significance. The presentation of the case offers an unusual longitudinal perspective of over four decades, illustrating the variable expressivity and long-term outcome of KIF11 disorders. This report calls for the consideration of KIF11 variants in the differential diagnosis of syndromic developmental delay and microcephaly in adults and underlines the diagnostic as well as the prognostic importance of detailed genetic and phenotypic analysis, particularly in cases with de novo variants.
papers.what_happened: A case report describes a 42-year-old woman with a de novo KIF11 in-frame deletion presenting with microcephaly, chorioretinopathy, lymphedema, and intellectual disability (MCLID syndrome), documented over a 40-year follow-up.
papers.why_it_matters: KIF11 is one of the established genetic causes of primary lymphedema tracked in this taxonomy; adult MCLID presentations are underreported, so this adds rare natural-history data on variable expressivity and long-term course.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is a single case report with no comparator or generalizable data — it describes one patient's course, not a population-level finding.

papers.title: Lymphedema and Alzheimer's Disease: Connecting Through the "Peripheral-Central Lymphatic System".
papers.abstract: The connection between the peripheral lymphatic system (PLS) and the central lymphatic system (CLS) plays a crucial role for the overall circulatory system. Notably, there are several similarities between lymphedema and Alzheimer's disease (AD). Accumulating evidence suggests that lymphedema might be associated with AD, potentially influencing its progression through mechanisms related to the peripheral-central lymphatic circulation. This review summarizes the lymphatic system's structure, function, and drainage pathways, emphasizing how aging and blockage of the CLS can exacerbate the progression of AD. Additionally, we discuss the relationship between lymphedema and AD, highlighting the significance of the PLS-CLS and exploring lymphaticovenous anastomosis as a promising treatment for both lymphedema and AD.
papers.what_happened: A narrative review proposes mechanistic links between the peripheral and central lymphatic systems and discusses lymphaticovenous anastomosis as a candidate shared treatment concept for both lymphedema and Alzheimer's disease.
papers.why_it_matters: It offers a speculative but novel cross-disciplinary framework connecting lymphatic drainage physiology to neurodegeneration research.
papers.what_limits_confidence: This is a narrative review synthesizing existing literature with no new primary data, and it does not specify whether the lymphedema it discusses is primary or secondary.

papers.title: Ophthalmic Manifestations of KIF11-Associated Microcephaly With or Without Chorioretinopathy, Lymphedema, or Intellectual Disability: A Case Report of a Novel Variant
papers.journal: The American Journal of Case Reports
papers.abstract: Case report of a 39-year-old man from Saudi Arabia with retinitis pigmentosa and a novel heterozygous frameshift variant in KIF11 (NM_004523.4: c.535del; p.(Ser179Leufs*16)), classified as likely pathogenic. The variant was absent from population databases and not previously reported. The patient was diagnosed with KIF11-related microcephaly, lymphedema, chorioretinopathy, mental retardation (MCLMR) syndrome, presenting with microcephaly and chorioretinal atrophy but without lymphedema at exam. Due to reduced penetrance, individuals with KIF11 mutations may present with only a subset of the syndrome's features.
papers.what_happened: A case report describes a novel, previously unreported KIF11 frameshift variant in a patient with retinitis pigmentosa, expanding the known variant spectrum of KIF11-related MCLMR syndrome.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds one data point to the phenotype spectrum of KIF11-associated primary lymphedema (MCLMR), relevant for genetic counseling given the gene's reduced penetrance.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single case report (n=1) with no lymphedema present on exam in this particular patient, so the finding is a genetic/phenotype-spectrum observation rather than lymphedema-specific clinical evidence.
key_findings: Novel heterozygous frameshift KIF11 variant (c.535del) classified as likely pathogenic, absent from population databases
Patient presented with microcephaly and chorioretinal atrophy consistent with MCLMR syndrome, illustrating reduced penetrance (no lymphedema in this case)
Reinforces that KIF11-MCLMR patients may present with only a subset of the syndrome's classic features

papers.title: Novel Ultrasound Technique for Assessing Fibrosis in Subcutaneous Fat in Lymphedematous Limbs.
papers.abstract: There is no standardized method for identifying fibrosis in the subcutaneous tissue of lymphedematous limbs. This study evaluated the relationship between ultrasonographic findings and fibrosis severity in patients with lower limb lymphedema. A retrospective analysis included 92 sites in 40 limbs of 26 female patients undergoing lymphaticovenous anastomosis. Skin thickness and subcutaneous echogenicity were assessed preoperatively using an 18-MHz linear ultrasound probe and classified into four grades (U0-U3). Fibrosis severity was evaluated intraoperatively and classified into five grades (F0-F4). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis determined the diagnostic accuracy of skin thickness for predicting severe fibrosis (F3/F4), and a regression model was developed to predict fibrosis severity. Skin thickness was significantly greater in the calves (2.7 mm) than in the thighs (2.1 mm, p < 0.01) and increased with lymphedema stage. Fibrosis severity was higher above the superficial fascia and more prevalent in calves (p < 0.01). ROC analysis showed an area under the curve of 0.80 for calf (above the superficial fascia), with a cutoff of 2.65 mm. The regression model (R2 = 0.51, p < 0.001) demonstrated that skin thickness and fat echogenicity significantly predicted fibrosis severity. Ultrasound-based measurements of skin thickness and fat echogenicity are reliable and noninvasive predictors of fibrosis severity in patients with lymphedema. These findings support the use of ultrasound imaging to guide treatment planning and improve surgical outcomes. However, further validation is needed in diverse populations.
papers.what_happened: A retrospective study of 26 patients (40 limbs, 92 sites) undergoing lymphaticovenous anastomosis for lower limb lymphedema found that preoperative ultrasound measurements of skin thickness and fat echogenicity predicted intraoperatively-graded subcutaneous fibrosis severity (AUC 0.80, R²=0.51).
papers.why_it_matters: A validated noninvasive ultrasound score could help clinicians stage fibrosis severity and plan surgical candidacy before committing to lymphaticovenous anastomosis, without relying on the current gold standard of intraoperative visual grading.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-center retrospective series with only 26 patients and no independent validation cohort, and the study population's primary-vs-secondary lymphedema etiology is not specified.

papers.title: Ultrasonographic Evaluations of Tendons/Fascia in Lower Limb Lymphedema and Lipedema.
papers.journal: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate ultrasonographic changes in lower extremity tendons and plantar fascia of patients with chronic edema and their relationship with edema volume, pain, function, and quality of life. DESIGN: This observational case-control study included 53 patients with chronic lower extremity edema and 55 age- and sex-matched controls. Ultrasonography assessed the Achilles, tibialis posterior, peroneal, and patellar tendons and plantar fascia. Edema volume was calculated from limb circumferences. Outcomes included the Lower Extremity Functional Scale (LEFS), Lymphedema Quality of Life Questionnaire-Leg (LYMQOL-Leg), and Visual Analogue Scale (VAS). RESULTS: All tendons (except the patellar tendon) and plantar fascia were thicker in the edema group than controls (P<0.05). Differences in Achilles tendon and plantar fascia thickness remained significant after BMI adjustment (all P<0.01) and correlated positively with edema volume (P<0.05). Plantar fasciitis (50.9%) and Achilles tendinopathy (22.6%) were more frequent in the edema group (P<0.05). Patients had lower LEFS and higher LYMQOL-Leg and VAS scores (all P<0.01). CONCLUSION: Chronic lower extremity edema was associated with alterations in tendon and fascial morphology, particularly the Achilles tendon and plantar fascia. Musculoskeletal ultrasonography may complement clinical evaluation by providing information regarding tendon and fascial involvement.
papers.what_happened: A case-control study of 53 patients with chronic lower-extremity edema (lymphedema and lipedema pooled, etiology and primary-vs-secondary status unspecified) versus 55 matched controls found thicker Achilles tendons and plantar fascia on ultrasound, correlated with edema volume and remaining significant after BMI adjustment.
papers.why_it_matters: Suggests chronic limb edema is associated with measurable tendon/fascial changes and higher rates of plantar fasciitis and Achilles tendinopathy, which could inform why some lymphedema patients report musculoskeletal pain and prompt consideration of ultrasound assessment.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Lymphedema and lipedema patients were pooled without separating by etiology (primary vs secondary lymphedema unspecified), it is a cross-sectional association (not a treatment or longitudinal study), and the tendon/fascia findings are surrogate imaging measures rather than patient-important outcomes.

papers.title: Sex, age, and body mass index as predictors of lymphovenous anastomosis and vascularized lymph node transfer outcomes: A multicenter cohort study.
papers.journal: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery
papers.abstract: Retrospective multicenter cohort study of a prospectively maintained lymphedema database (2016-2025) examining associations of sex, age, and BMI with long-term outcomes after LVA or VLNT for chronic extremity lymphedema. Male patients showed significantly greater treatment response in lower-extremity lymphedema at 12/24 months after LVA and 12 months after VLNT. Higher BMI was associated with less favorable response after upper-extremity VLNT at 12/18 months, with no consistent BMI effect in the lower extremity. Age showed no consistent effect. Neither variable significantly affected postoperative complication rates.
papers.what_happened: A retrospective multicenter cohort study of patients undergoing LVA or VLNT for chronic extremity lymphedema (2016-2025) found male sex was associated with better treatment response in lower-extremity LVA/VLNT, higher BMI predicted worse response after upper-extremity VLNT, and age had no consistent effect.
papers.why_it_matters: Adds to sparse evidence on which patient characteristics predict surgical lymphedema treatment response, potentially informing patient selection and counseling.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Retrospective, single-arm (no non-surgical comparator) design with surrogate volumetric endpoints; lymphedema etiology (primary vs. secondary) is not specified in the available abstract, and the authors themselves describe the results as preliminary requiring validation.
key_findings: Male sex associated with greater treatment response after lower-extremity LVA (12, 24mo) and VLNT (12mo)
Higher BMI associated with worse response after upper-extremity VLNT (12, 18mo) but not lower-extremity
Age showed no consistent association with outcomes
No effect of sex/BMI/age on postoperative complication rates (Clavien-Dindo)

papers.title: [Giant Scrotal Elephantiasis as a Septic Focus in Generalized Lymphedema: Radical Resection Following Initial Suspicion of Malignancy].
papers.abstract: Case report of massive scrotal elephantiasis, generalized lymphedema, and septic deterioration in a non-endemic region, initially raising suspicion of a malignant soft tissue tumor. Describes diagnostic pitfalls and radical surgical resection under a persistent septic setting.
papers.what_happened: A case report describes a patient with massive scrotal elephantiasis and generalized lymphedema in a non-endemic region, initially suspected to be malignant, managed with radical surgical resection after septic deterioration.
papers.why_it_matters: Illustrates a rare, severe presentation and the diagnostic pitfalls of distinguishing extreme lymphedema-related swelling from malignancy in surgical decision-making.
papers.what_limits_confidence: Single-patient case report with no stated etiology (primary vs. secondary/idiopathic) for the underlying generalized lymphedema and no generalizable treatment data.
key_findings: Massive scrotal elephantiasis plus generalized lymphedema plus sepsis initially mimicked a malignant soft tissue tumor
Managed with radical surgical resection
Etiology of the underlying generalized lymphedema not specified in the abstract

papers.title: Impaired lymphatic drainage in a child with hydrops fetalis and a novel variant in the PROX1 gene: case report and review of literature.
papers.abstract: Case report of a preterm neonate born at 32 weeks with non-immune hydrops fetalis, congenital bilateral chylothorax and chylous ascites requiring peritoneal dialysis, who died at approximately seven months of age. Clinical exome sequencing identified a novel heterozygous PROX1 variant c.502C>T, p.(Arg168Trp). Accompanied by a literature review of PROX1 in human lymphatic development.
papers.novelty_assessment: PROX1 is the master regulator of lymphatic endothelial identity but is only rarely reported as a monogenic cause of human lymphatic disease; a novel de novo-type missense variant with a lethal generalized lymphatic phenotype is a genuine addition to a very thin human variant catalog.
key_findings: Novel heterozygous PROX1 missense variant c.502C>T p.(Arg168Trp) identified by clinical exome sequencing in a preterm neonate.
Phenotype comprised non-immune hydrops fetalis, congenital bilateral chylothorax and chylous ascites; the child died at ~7 months.
No functional validation of the variant is reported; pathogenicity rests on rarity, in-silico prediction and phenotype fit.
papers.clinical_implications: Supports including PROX1 on gene panels for non-immune hydrops/congenital chylothorax of unexplained cause. Does not establish a genotype-prognosis relationship from n=1.

papers.title: RAS Inhibitor RMC-7977 Blocks Vascular Overgrowth of NRAS-Mutant Endothelial Cells
papers.journal: Journal of Cellular and Molecular Medicine
papers.abstract: RAS mutations occur in patients with several types of vascular anomalies, but effective treatments remain limited. This study evaluated the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor RMC-7977 in human endothelial cells expressing mutant NRAS, assessing effects on vascular overgrowth phenotypes.
papers.novelty_assessment: First report applying a pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor to endothelial cells carrying a vascular-anomaly NRAS mutation. Directly relevant to RAS-driven complex lymphatic anomalies, where MEK inhibition is the current off-label standard and does not work in all patients.
key_findings: RMC-7977, a RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor, reduced overgrowth phenotypes in human endothelial cells expressing mutant NRAS.
Proposes upstream RAS inhibition as an alternative to downstream MEK inhibition for RAS-mutant vascular/lymphatic anomalies.
Cell-culture level only; no animal efficacy or human data reported in the abstract.
papers.clinical_implications: Pipeline-relevant only. Provides a preclinical rationale for testing RAS(ON) inhibitors in RAS-mutant complex lymphatic anomalies, a population in which trametinib failures are documented (see SHOC2 report this cycle). No clinical inference is warranted.

papers.title: Macrocystic lymphatic malformation of the gluteal region complicated by abscess formation: the crucial role of multimodal imaging in pediatric emergency care - case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: Case report of a 2-year-old girl with a known macrocystic lymphatic malformation of the gluteal region who developed superinfection after minor blunt trauma, described through sequential ultrasound and contrast-enhanced MRI.
papers.novelty_assessment: Single case; infection of a macrocystic lymphatic malformation after trauma is a recognised complication, not a new observation.
key_findings: Superinfection of a known macrocystic lymphatic malformation followed minor blunt trauma in a 2-year-old.
Serial ultrasound (increasing cyst-wall vascularity at 72h) plus contrast-enhanced MRI guided the diagnosis.
papers.clinical_implications: Reinforces existing practice: infection is a known complication of lymphatic malformations and serial imaging can distinguish it from lesion growth. Not practice-changing.

papers.title: Omental Cysts in the Pediatric Population: Diagnostic Challenges and Surgical Outcomes.
papers.journal: Journal of Indian Association of Pediatric Surgeons
papers.abstract: Retrospective single-department review (2015-2024) of nine children (median age 4 years) who underwent omentectomy for omental cysts, a rare intra-abdominal lymphatic malformation accounting for approximately 2% of intra-abdominal lymphatic lesions. Presentation was usually abdominal pain or distension; preoperative diagnosis was frequently uncertain.
papers.novelty_assessment: Small institutional case series of a rare abdominal lymphatic malformation subtype; descriptive, no new mechanism or comparative outcome.
key_findings: Nine children underwent omentectomy for omental cysts over a decade at one department.
Preoperative diagnosis was often unclear because clinical and radiological features are nonspecific.
No comparator group; outcome reporting is descriptive.
papers.clinical_implications: Supports keeping omental cyst in the differential of pediatric abdominal pain/distension. Too small and uncontrolled to inform operative choice.
